data.narrative:
Netrasemi is a Series A-stage semiconductor design company founded by Jyothis Indirabhai, Deepa Geetha, and Sreejith Varma, having raised ₹107 Cr (~$13M) to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers operating at Series A and adjacent stages, including Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Positron AI.

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yields $26M. Peer-median anchoring across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comps—Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B)—produces a median of $2.0B, with a floor of $1.0B and ceiling of $2.3B. Public-comp P/S anchoring was not applied; the semiconductor sector median P/S of 18.9x across the three public comparables cannot be meaningfully deployed without Netrasemi's disclosed revenue, which is unavailable for private companies at this stage.

The triangulated range spans $22M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The extreme width reflects a structural tension: stage-progression suggests $26M, while peer multiples imply $1.0B–$2.3B. Key uncertainties include Netrasemi's relative technical differentiation within the peer set and actual revenue traction versus peer benchmarks.
